items.prompt: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. What is its area?

options.why: 90 = 9 × 10. Each side is 9 cm, so use 9 × 9.
108 = 36 × 3. Find the length of a side first.

hints: Find the length of one side.
A square has 4 equal sides.
Each side is 36 ÷ 4 cm.
items.explanation: Each side is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm, so the area is 9 × 9 = 81 cm².

items.prompt: A rectangle is 12 cm long and 8 cm wide. The midpoints of its four sides are joined to make a rhombus. What is the area of the rhombus?

figure.alt: A rectangle 12 cm long and 8 cm wide. The middle points of its four sides are joined to make a rhombus inside it.

options.why: 24 cm² is only a quarter of the rectangle.
Cut the rectangle into 4 smaller rectangles and look at each one.
64 cm² is 8 × 8. The rhombus is exactly half the rectangle.

hints: Draw the two lines that join opposite midpoints.
They cut the rectangle into 4 small rectangles.
Each side of the rhombus cuts one small rectangle exactly in half.
items.explanation: Joining opposite midpoints makes 4 small rectangles, and the rhombus takes exactly half of each one. So the rhombus is half the rectangle: 12 × 8 ÷ 2 = 48 cm².

solution.say: The rhombus covers half of each quarter.

items.prompt: A 4 × 4 × 4 cube is painted on the outside. It is cut into 64 small cubes. How many small cubes have no paint at all?

figure.alt: A big cube made of 64 small cubes, 4 along each edge, painted on the outside.

options.why: The cubes deep inside are never touched by the paint.
1 centre cube is the answer for a 3 × 3 × 3 cube. This cube is bigger.
The unpainted cubes form a cube 2 small cubes along each edge.
6 is the number of faces, not of hidden cubes.

hints: Unpainted cubes are hidden inside.
Remove the outside layer from every face.
Each edge of the hidden cube is 4 - 2 small cubes long.
items.explanation: Taking away the outside layer on every face leaves an inner cube 2 small cubes along each edge. It has 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 small cubes, none painted.

solution.say: Remove 1 layer from both ends of each edge.

items.prompt: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 2:30?

figure.alt: A clock showing 2:30. The minute hand points to 6. The hour hand is halfway between 2 and 3.

options.why: The hour hand is not on 3. It is halfway between 2 and 3.
Each hour mark is 30°, so half a mark is 15°.
120° is the angle from 2 to 6, but the hour hand has moved past 2.

hints: Each hour mark is 30°.
At 2:30 the hour hand is halfway between 2 and 3.
From the hour hand to the 6 is three and a half hour marks.
items.explanation: The minute hand is on 6. The hour hand is halfway between 2 and 3, which is 3.5 hour marks from the 6. The angle is 3.5 × 30° = 105°.

items.prompt: A rectangle has an area of 36 cm². Its sides are whole numbers of centimetres. What is the largest possible perimeter?
hints: List the pairs of whole numbers that multiply to 36.
The pairs are 1 and 36, 2 and 18, 3 and 12, 4 and 9, 6 and 6.
A long, thin rectangle has the biggest perimeter.
items.explanation: The longest, thinnest rectangle is 36 cm by 1 cm. Its perimeter is 36 + 1 + 36 + 1 = 74 cm.

items.prompt: A box is 30 cm long, 20 cm wide and 10 cm tall. How many cubes with sides of 10 cm fit exactly inside it?

options.why: The box is only 10 cm tall, so there is just one layer.
60 is 30 + 20 + 10. Count how many cubes fit along each edge.
600 is the volume divided by 10. Each cube is 10 × 10 × 10.

hints: Find how many cubes fit along each edge.
Along 30 cm fit 3 cubes. Along 20 cm fit 2 cubes.
The box is 10 cm tall, so how many layers are there?
items.explanation: 3 cubes fit along the length, 2 along the width and 1 up the height. That is 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 cubes.

items.prompt: A square is cut into 3 equal rectangles. Each rectangle has a perimeter of 24 cm. What is the perimeter of the square?

figure.alt: A square cut into 3 equal thin rectangles by 2 straight lines.

hints: Call the side of the square 3 parts.
Each rectangle is 3 parts long and 1 part wide.
The perimeter of one rectangle is 3 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 8 parts.
items.explanation: Each rectangle is 3 parts long and 1 part wide, so its perimeter is 8 parts = 24 cm. One part is 3 cm, the square's side is 9 cm, and its perimeter is 36 cm.

items.prompt: A rectangle 6 squares long and 4 squares high is drawn on squared paper. A straight line goes from one corner to the opposite corner. How many squares does the line pass through?

figure.alt: A grid 6 squares long and 4 squares high. A straight line goes from the bottom left corner to the top right corner.

hints: The line passes through a grid corner exactly halfway along.
Look at one half: a 3 by 2 rectangle with its own diagonal.
In a 3 by 2 rectangle, count the squares the diagonal crosses.
items.explanation: The diagonal passes through the grid corner at the centre, so it splits into two diagonals of 3 by 2 rectangles. Each of those crosses 4 squares, so the whole line crosses 4 + 4 = 8 squares.

solution.say: The line passes the grid corner at the middle, 3 across and 2 up.
In a 3 by 2 rectangle the line starts in 1 square and enters a new one at each grid line it crosses.

items.prompt: A garden is 20 m long and 12 m wide. A path 1 m wide runs all the way round the inside edge. What is the area of the path?

figure.alt: A rectangular garden 20 m long and 12 m wide, with a path 1 m wide along the inside of its edge.

hints: Find the area of the whole garden.
Inside the path is a smaller rectangle. Each side is 2 m shorter.
The inner rectangle is 18 m by 10 m.
items.explanation: The garden is 20 × 12 = 240 m². Inside the path is 18 × 10 = 180 m². So the path is 240 - 180 = 60 m².

solution.say: Inside the path: 1 m off each end.
